decisions.reason: The existing rule covers conveying verbatim Program source code as received and all four cumulative notice and recipient-license requirements (§4, line 69).
The existing rule covers charging any price, including no price, for each verbatim copy conveyed under §4 (line 70).
Section 4 separately permits offering support or warranty protection for a fee (line 70). The existing Charge rule covers the price of a verbatim copy, not a fee for support or warranty protection.

The existing rule covers the same source-form conveyance, applicable §4 conditions, modification and date notices, license notice, whole-work licensing, and the interactive-interface exception (§5, lines 73–77).
The existing Combine rule captures the aggregate boundary and conditions, including that inclusion does not extend the License to other aggregate parts (§5, line 78).
The existing rule covers object-code conveyance, applicable §§4–5 conditions, and the requirement to convey machine-readable Corresponding Source by one §6 alternative (line 81).
The existing rule captures the physical-product object-code method and accompanying Corresponding Source on the specified durable customary medium (§6(a), line 82).
The existing rule covers the written offer, its duration, eligible source-copy or no-charge network-access alternatives, and the physical-copy price cap (§6(b), line 83).
The existing rule covers occasional, noncommercial conveyance, receipt of object code with a §6(b) offer, and the offer-copy alternative (§6(c), line 84).
The existing rule covers equivalent same-place access at no further charge, the conditional different-server directions requirement, and continued source availability (§6(d), line 85).
The existing rule covers informing peers where the object code and Corresponding Source are offered publicly at no charge under §6(d) (§6(e), line 86).
The existing rule captures the exception for a separable object-code portion whose source is excluded from Corresponding Source as a System Library (§6, line 87).

The existing rule accurately covers the qualifying User Product transaction and Installation Information duty, with the exception when neither the conveyor nor a third party can install modified object code (§6, line 93). The candidate’s requires expression incorrectly makes the duty alternative depend on that exception; the existing rule preserves the source’s meaning.

The existing rule captures the same network-access denial grounds: the modification itself must materially and adversely affect network operation or violate communication rules and protocols (§6, line 95).

The existing rule’s source excerpt and scope state that Installation Information does not require continued support, warranty, or updates for recipient-modified or recipient-installed work or product (§6, line 95); the candidate adds no separate affirmative source duty.

The existing ProvideSource rule covers both Corresponding Source and Installation Information, including the publicly documented format, public source-code implementation, and no-special-password-or-key requirements (§6, line 97).

additions.source_excerpt: You may charge any price or no price for each copy that you convey, and you may offer support or warranty protection for a fee.
additions.scope_note: AGPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0-or-later, section 4; the conveyor may offer support or warranty protection for a fee.
additions.condition_explanation: The permission is to charge a fee for offered support or warranty protection; it is not a duty to offer either.
